messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: zero sum probe effects
parts:
Hi, I saw in the documentation somewhere that the probe effects (per
unit, I guess) must sum to zero. I am fitting effects that will not do
this in general. Am I going to get an error, or will I be just violating
protocal but it will go ahead and do it anyway. Or worse, will it
silently force them to sum to zero? Thanks, Elizabeth

If you grab the source and look in RmaPlm.R you'll see that
getFitFunction() does enforce the sum constraint, but if you're defining
your own class with its own fit function you should be able to do as you
please with probe effects.

Cheers,

Ken

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: zero sum probe effects
parts:
Hi,

yes that constraint is mentioned in the documentation for the
ProbeLevelModel class. The main reason for "enforcing" that is so
that parameter estimates from similar models like the multiplicative
(MBEI) and the log-additive (RMA) models are on the same scale and
directly comparable. If you look at the BioC code and elsewhere
different implementations use different constraint to make these
models identifiable, which just adds confusion.

Basically what I am asking for is that if you need to set a constraint
on PLM for its parameters to be identifiable, then please follow the
aroma.affymetrix standard where probe affinities multiplies to one on
the natural scale (or sum to zero on the log scale). To the best of
my knowledge, and as Ken writes, there are no enforcement (or
rescaling) on this in the code.

It sounds like you don't have a problem of making your parameters
identifiable at the unit group level; do you make them identifiable at
the unit level instead? I've been thinking of extending the class
structure with a TwoWayPlm level where the above constraints would
come in. Maybe you need a ThreeWayPlm? If you have better names for
this, please tell me.

To summarize, for now I think it is safe for you to do what you do,
but should at some point be harmonized.

Cheers

Henrik
